CIT^ OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes

n
  December 1, 2025 - 5:30 P.M.
  Pasadena Convention Center
  300 E Green St, Pasadena, CA 91101

  SPECIAL WORKSHOP MEETING

  OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the special meeting to order at 5:59 p.m.
  (Absent: None)

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Rick Cole
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  CITY COUNCIL BUDGET WORKSHOP ON ISSUES INCLUDING,
  BUT NOT LIMITED TO, DISCUSSION OF CITY BUDGET, CITY
  COUNCIL BUDGET PRIORITIES, CRITERIA FOR
  PRIORITIZATION, MID-YEAR ADJUSTMENT PROTOCOLS, AND
  OTHER MATTERS IDENTIFIED BY MEMBERS OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL

  City Manager Marquez provided introductory comments on the item.
  He also introduced Karin Schnaider as the new Director of Finance
  and welcomed her to the City.

  Phillip Leclair, Chief Information Officer, provided introductory
  remarks on the item, provided details on his role as the workshop
  facilitator, and outlined the process for the City Council budget
  priorities discussion.

  Matt hlawkesworth provided a Powerpoint presentation and reported
  on budgetary changes to CalPERS, pension increases, debt
  refinancing, processing fees, and developing goals and outcomes
  for fee-for-service programs. He also reported that City staff is
  analyzing upcoming funding cuts from the federal government, more
  specifically noting that housing, public health, and work force
  development programs are slated for federal funding reductions.

  The following individuals advocated for the City to allocate funds for
  housing services for unhoused residents and/or provided comments
  related to the need for interim housing:

  Council Minutes  1  12/01/2025
   Sonja Berndt, Pasadena resident
  Joanne Long, Pasadena resident

n  Rex Mayreis, Pasadena 100, advocated for the City Council
  to prioritize funding for projects to achieve the City's adopted
  goal of Carbon Free by 2030.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that one letter advocating for the City
  Council to include Complete Streets & Street Safety Improvement
  Projects as part of the City's budget priorities, and one letter
  advocating for the City Council to improve its budget hearing process
  to provide greater transparency to the public, were received by the
  City Clerk's Office, posted online, and made part of the public record.

  The City Council participated in a discussion regarding the criteria
  presented by City staff for setting goals and budget priorities, as well
  as the need for adding equity as one of the criteria to consider in the
  City's budgeting process. City staff and members of the City Council
  noted the importance of creating and maintaining a flexible budget
  that aligns with the City Council's priorities, while being able to shift
  and make real-time decisions to address critical needs (i.e., Eaton
  Canyon Fire response) when necessary.

  Following staff's review of the 21 identified budget priorities, as well
  as a consensus building exercise by members of the City Council to
  narrow priorities to specific programs and services (which were later
  consolidated under programmatic themes), the City Council
  Councilmember Madison
  excused himself and left
  identified the following as top budget priorities:
  the meeting at 7:09 p.m.
  Theme: Making City Roads Safer
  • Roadways/Pavement Condition Index Improvements
  • Traffic Enforcement
  • Pedestrian, Bicyclist and Motorist Safety

  Theme: Invest in Housing People, Homelessness Prevention
  • Year-Round Homelessness Shelter
  • Homeless Transitional/Temporary Housing

  Theme: Fire Preparedness
  • Fire Department Facilities Upgrades & Training Center

  Theme: Community-Centered Economic Development
  • Economic Development Strategic Plan Implementation,
  Business Retention
  • Implement Neighborhood Specific Plans

  Council Minutes  2  12/01/2025
   Theme: Climate Change
  • Carbon-Free Electricity Transition - Resolution No. 9977

  Other priorities receiving medium support included:
  • Sustain Essential Programs When Grant Funding is Reduced
  or Terminated
  • Debris Removal (Public Right-of-Way Clean Up)

  The City Council continued its discussion on the priorities identified
  in the consensus building exercise, and provided suggestions on the
  various ways that staff can act on the City Council's programmatic
  themes and projects, including pursuit of alternative funding sources,
  and for staff to do the research and provide recommendations to City
  Council on how to best achieve outcomes in line with Council's
  agreed upon priorities. The City Council and staff further discussed
  improving business practices without having to allocate additional
  funding for certain services provided by the City, focusing on
  business retention in the City, and creating and focusing on
  meaningful performance measures that illustrate community benefits
  of City services and programs.

  City staff noted that the budget discussion will continue as part of
  Phase 2 of this effort, with staff to come back to the City Council and
  provide more input on moving the process forward, as well as
  responding to questions raised.

  The City Council expressed its appreciation to City staff for the
  opportunity to provide input on budget priorities at the outset of the
  City's budget process, and for the well-executed budget planning
  workshop.

ADJOURNMENT  Following discussion, on order of the Mayor, by the consensus of the
  City Council, the special meeting of the City Council adjourned at
  8:09 p.r

  ^.
  Victor M. Gordo, Mayor
  City of Pasadena
